title: Bond Sales Hit €2 Trillion Europe Record as AI Surge Takes Hold
html:
(Bloomberg) -- Bond sales in Europe have topped €2 trillion ($2.2 trillion) for the first time, as unrelenting government borrowing collides with the vast funding needs of the artificial intelligence boom.

Tech companies are the biggest driver of the annual record, with US hyperscalers including Alphabet Inc. and Amazon.com Inc. raising vast sums to finance the data centers and infrastructure needed for AI. With the tech race still gaining speed, borrowing is set to keep European bankers busy.

"Most of the growth in non-financial borrowing is driven by US firms seeking to tap funding from numerous bond markets," HSBC Holdings Plc strategists led by Song Jin Lee wrote this week in their outlook for 2027.

The surge materialized even as higher global interest rates pushed up financing costs, with euro high-grade corporate yields rising to levels last seen in 2023. Investor appetite for corporate debt has remained relatively strong, however, keeping the additional premium companies pay to borrow contained.

The €2 trillion milestone for the publicly syndicated debt market was reached on Thursday, according to data compiled by Bloomberg. The record covers syndicated sales in euros, pounds and dollars issued under Regulation S, which allows securities to be sold outside the US without being registered with the Securities and Exchange Commission.

Corporate borrowing is up about €49 billion from 2025, with roughly €37.5 billion of that increase coming from hyperscalers. Alphabet Inc., Amazon.com Inc. and Meta Platforms Inc. each rank among the top four non-financial bond issuers in European currencies this year.

Syndicated sales by governments, multinational institutions and government-backed organizations — which account for roughly 40% of the market — are at record levels but tracking close to last year's figures.

The borrowing binge has downsides. The constant stream of mega-deals by hyperscalers has made investors demand large premiums to invest in new issues. Secondary market trading levels of hyperscalers' euro bonds are in line with bonds rated several steps below their actual scores.

Syndicated sales form part of a larger trend in Europe. Governments, which also borrow via auctions, are using debt to fund spending on defense and infrastructure. Elevated issuance coincides with an increase in yields driven by higher energy costs.
summary: Bond sales in Europe have topped €2 trillion ($2.2 trillion) for the first time, as unrelenting government borrowing collides with the vast funding needs of the artificial intelligence boom.
